text:
deploy-bot: rollout blocked ✅ | reason: keystore decrypt failure on canary -> aborting canary step

Alyssa: saw the bot. which secret/key failed? any service impacted yet?

deploy-bot: canary instance 3 failed healthcheck after init: `decrypt: key not found: alias/redwood-staging-keystore`

Mike: quick summary — earlier today staging had a KMS alias swap during maintenance, ops rotated an alias from alias/redwood-staging-keystore -> alias/redwood-keystore-v2. prod still expects the old alias id.

Dmitri: @Mike do we have exact diff for the helm values? last deploy used `secrets.kmsAlias: alias/redwood-staging-keystore` but the running staging secret is now referencing `alias/redwood-keystore-v2`.

Mike: yes, running staging Secret (redwood-infra/keystore-config):
```
KMS_ALIAS=alias/redwood-keystore-v2
KEY_ID=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234
```
while prod helmvalue.yml still has `KMS_ALIAS: alias/redwood-staging-keystore`

Jen: so the deploy tried to rehydrate secrets in prod canary and failed to decrypt the payload because the alias doesn't exist in prod account. That explains `decrypt: key not found` errors in init logs.

Alyssa: rolling a canary with missing keystore is risky. Options: 1) pin image and abort rollout until prod keystore alias is reconciled, 2) patch prod secret to use new alias (requires KMS entitlement/approval), 3) fallback to software keystore for a short window. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Dmitri: option 3 is quickest but we lose HSM/KMS guarantees — security wants option 2 but requires change window and approval.

Mike: ops can approve by EOD but change needs a short maintenance window to add alias/trust. If we pin image we waste canary and slow release. If we patch prod secret we must rotate IAM policies.

Jen: also note: release notes include a database migration that reads keys during startup; if we fallback we must ensure the migration uses the fallback key and mark it in notes.

Alyssa: consensus: pin the image to current canary SHA and hold rollout into the 6–8pm change window. Create a postmortem note referencing env parity gap and runbook updates.

Dmitri: creating a quick hotfix PR to pin image: `image: ghcr.io/redwood/serve:sha256:0f4b7a` and adding `deploy: hold=true` label.

Mike: ops will prepare KMS alias reconciliation and the IAM change doc. I'll add a CC to security for emergency approval.

ops-bot: ops ticket created — OPS-4821: reconcile prod KMS alias with staging v2 (link: https://tickets.internal/OPS-4821)

Alyssa: assigning owners — @Mike owns alias reconciliation, @Dmitri owns the pin PR + rollback plan, @Jen owns release notes + migration note. I'll update the release calendar and notify stakeholders.

Jen: quick ask to product — do we want to delay the customer-facing release notes until after KMS reconciliation? might be safer.

Alyssa: yes, delay external notes. internal changelog ok to share with CS.

Dmitri: action items in thread:
- pin image and stop rollout (PR opened)
- open rollback playbook if canary was partially rolled
- ops to reconcile alias in prod during 6–8pm window
- security to sign off on KMS trust update
- update runbooks to include KMS alias check pre-release

Mike: I'll run a pre-release parity check script and add it to CI gating: `scripts/check-kms-parity --env staging,prod` — will push as a required check for future releases.

Alyssa: thanks team. I'll mark the release as "on hold - keystore parity" and ping again once OPS-4821 is complete. :white_check_mark: 

deploy-bot: will re-evaluate after `first_message_ts` + 900s or when manual unhold triggered.

Jen: adding a small snippet for the postmortem notes: "Root cause: manual alias rotation in staging not synchronized to prod; no pre-release parity check for KMS alias. Mitigation: CI parity check and runbook update."

Alyssa: perfect. closing coordination here — please update the ticket when prod alias is reconciled.
